minutes.headline: Steering committee reorganized with Tim as chair and Jerry as clerk, but the consultant was absent and the plan's status stayed unclear.
minutes.summary: The Master Plan Steering Committee met for its first official meeting since May of last year. It filled the chair and clerk positions by roll call vote, leaving vice chair open. Members spent most of the time questioning the consultant's survey and outreach work and the contract's deliverables, and planned to get the consultant and the planning board chair to the next meeting and to get more boards represented.

public_comment.topic: Wants a master plan for town facilities, serves on the municipal building design committee, and asked to join the steering committee; was told to email the chair.
public_comment.stated_role: resident, member of the Lunenburg municipal building design committee

public_comment.topic: Questioned how the Ritter building cafe idea fits the municipal building plan and how a vocational program could be funded; asked when such questions are discussed.

Called for historic commission or architectural preservation district representation, wider circulation of the survey matrix to boards, and attention to affordable housing rules. Plans to apply for the open seat.
public_comment.stated_role: chair of the architectural preservation district commission

public_comment.topic: Defended the consultant and the contract, saying public engagement was fairly good and the plan should be finished.

votes.motion: Reorganize the committee with Tim as chair and Jerry as clerk, leaving vice chair open.

votes.outcome: passed, roll call with yes votes from the listed members; Kim had left

budget_items.what_was_said: A member said it is a large contract and asked for a memo on deliverables against the contract. Another member said it is a lot of money but possibly fully used per the statement of work.
A member said the statement of work lists up to a set number of meetings and fewer have been held. The contract ended in January.

decisions.decision: The chair will look into the process for appointing a member-at-large and asked the resident to email interest to him.
Members will reach out to other boards and commissions for input and to send one representative each to future meetings.
The chair will ask the planning board chair at next Monday's planning board meeting to attend the next meeting and will seek a check-in with the consultant.
Chris Riley will work with Annie in the town office to notify all boards and commissions about representation.
The chair will ask the consultant for information on affordable housing.
The chair will send a Doodle poll to schedule the next meeting.
The chair will bring a list of active members and vacant seats to the next meeting.
Tom (architectural preservation commission chair) will submit his application to the planning board chair for the open seat.

what_happened.line: The committee voted unanimously by roll call to reorganize, with Tim as chair and Jerry as clerk; the vice chair seat stayed open.
Members questioned the consultant's survey and outreach work, and one asked for a memo comparing the contract's deliverables with what was delivered.
A member noted the statement of work lists up to a set number of meetings, fewer have been held, and the contract ended in January.
Members agreed to ask other boards and commissions to send one representative each, with the town office to notify them.
The chair will ask the planning board chair to attend the next meeting and will seek a check-in with the consultant, who was absent.

why_it_matters: The master plan guides future zoning, housing and facilities decisions, and this meeting shows the committee has met rarely since May and has not yet established whether the plan is finished.
Whether the consultant's contract was fully used, and what was delivered under it, is still undetermined; the answer bears on whether more town money is needed to complete the plan.
